case.title: Backpressure
case.author_invariant: depth is exactly admitted requests minus effective drains, clamped to [0,2]. A full queue rejects without debit; a drain at zero is a no-op; every admission retains the canonical request payload.

worked_value.note: The third request is rejected at depth two. The drain releases one slot, so the fifth command is admitted.

story.premise: Once the bridge schedule is published, every department begins sending work into one two-slot handoff queue. A rejected request was never queued, and a drain from an empty queue cannot create future capacity. The controller must exert real backpressure while preserving each admitted command's public identity.
story.submission: Submit a bounded PULSE controller that admits exactly when current depth is below two, decrements only effective drains, and emits with zero added latency.
story.diagnostics: The exhaustive domain distinguishes over-admission, phantom debit on rejection, underflow on empty drain, ignored drain, delayed output, and payload substitution.
hints: A drain changes depth only when depth is positive.
